verdict.rationale: Many irs.gov guidance pages (EIN, SS-4, MeF, IRIS, Pub 525 update) appear in the pack with verbatim quoted content, which suggests the public reading surface returns readable static content. Probes of nonexistent irs.gov paths got ordinary 404s with a standard pipeline user agent rather than a challenge page. The only 403 observed was on an authenticated form-submission flow (/dmaf), and the 503 was on an application host, so neither concerns the guidance surface. Missing for 10: an explicit probe showing HTTP 200 on a guidance page with the standard user agent, confirmation that no CAPTCHA or bot challenge is served, and confirmation the pages render without JS.

support.subject: As an AI-native founder, the service's published guidance pages are reachable by a keyless agent with a standard identified user agent — no bot wall, JS-only shell, or CAPTCHA in front of the public reading surface
